## Inventory attachments

Connect to a repository and choose items. For restricted content, log in first
as described in the authentication vignette.

```{r inventory, eval=FALSE}
library(dspacer)
library(dplyr)

con <- ds_connect("https://repository.example.org/server/api")
items <- ds_get_items(con, query = "history")
files <- ds_get_files(con, items)
files
```

The inventory contains one row per item–bundle–bitstream association, including
filename, MIME type, size, checksum and primary-file status. It does not download
the file content.

The default bundle is `ORIGINAL`. To inventory all visible bundles instead:

```{r bundles, eval=FALSE}
all_files <- ds_get_files(con, items, bundles = NULL)
```

## Choose and retrieve text

Inspect the inventory and explicitly select the files you want. A Markdown file
may contain provenance or documentation rather than the document's text.
These filenames are illustrative, not package naming requirements:

```{r text, eval=FALSE}
selected <- files |>
  filter(name %in% c("transcription.md", "translation.md"))

texts <- ds_get_texts(con, selected)
```

The result contains both decoded `source_text` and analysis plaintext `text`,
along with file identifiers, SHA-256, retrieval time and conversion information.
File association uses UUIDs: identical filenames on different items are not
treated as the same attachment.

Markdown and UTF-8 plaintext are supported. The package does not perform OCR,
translation, language inference, stemming or automatic page-marker removal.
For encoding rules and exact Markdown rendering behaviour, see `?ds_get_texts`.

## Download original bytes

```{r download, eval=FALSE}
downloads <- ds_download(con, selected, "downloads")
downloads$local_path
```

This returns a manifest with local paths and hashes. Downloads use UUID-based
filenames and are checked against the repository's advertised size/checksum.
Conflicting local content is not silently overwritten. See `?ds_download` for
supported checksum algorithms and failure behaviour.

Downloads are buffered in memory and retrieved serially, so avoid very large
attachments. Restricted files remain sensitive local copies: secure their
storage and do not commit them or credentials.

## Save a dataset

```{r save, eval=FALSE}
metadata <- ds_get_metadata(items)
saveRDS(
  list(items = items, metadata = metadata, files = files, texts = texts),
  "repository_dataset.rds"
)
ds_disconnect(con)
```

Join tables using repository URL and UUIDs, not titles or filenames. Keep the
connection out of saved datasets because it contains sensitive session state.
